newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT DoCoMo in IPO, market cap seen at 5 trln yen.
newsitem.headline: NTT DoCoMo in IPO, market cap seen at 5 trln yen.

text.p: A maker of tiny mobile phones is about to make a lot of noise on the Tokyo bourse as NTT DoCoMo, a unit of telecoms giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT), gears up to offer its shares in the autumn of next year.

The initial public offering (IPO) for DoCoMo, with an estimated market capitalisation of about five trillion yen ($39.3 billion), is expected to be the largest share offer ever by a cellular phone operator.
Analysts doubted, however, that the offering would have a negative impact on the overall Tokyo stock market.
"DoCoMo's IPO will stimulate trading rather than negatively impact the supply-and-demand condition in the market," said Hiroyuki Iba, an analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
But analysts said the value of this hot IPO is difficult to predict as uncertainties still remain, such as whether new shares will also be issued.

The IPO is to be lead-managed by Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd, although a DoCoMo spokeswoman declined to confirm a Financial Times report on Thursday that Goldman Sachs & Co would also manage the offering.
NTT DoCoMo, as NTT Mobile Communications Network Inc is called, aims to list its shares as early as autumn of 1998, a company spokeswoman said. She declined to give any further details.
"The market capitalisation of the DoCoMo group will likely be five to six trillion yen ($47.2 billion)," said Toshiho Sato, an analyst at UBS Securities (East Asia) Ltd.

DKB's Iba said that the value of the first share sale by NTT DoCoMo next year will be as large as the Tokyo offering by German telecoms giant Deutsche Telekom when it made its debut in November last year.
The $13 billion global offering of Deutsche Telekom in Frankfurt, New York and Tokyo was second only to NTT's massive offering in 1987 and put 26 percent of the company's capital into public hands.
"Assuming that DoCoMo's market capitalisation will be five trillion yen ($39.3 billion), the total value of DoCoMo's IPO could be as large as one trillion yen ($7.8 billion)," Iba said.

DoCoMo, which already holds half of the Japanese mobile phone market at 10 million subscribers, is fast taking sales away from DDI Corp and other rivals on the strength of its strong brand name and nationwide network.

The wireless communications market in Japan was estimated to be worth 3.9 trillion yen ($30.7 billion) in the fiscal year through March 1997, up from 2.3 trillion yen ($18.1 billion) the year before, the Posts and Telecommunications Ministry said.
Another possible hitch to the IPO is NTT's dominant stake in the firm, which it has said it will not sell off.

Japan's anti-monopoly watchdog is seeking a sharp reduction in NTT's holdings in its cellular unit, stating that the telecom titan's control over the country's top cell phone operator is not desirable from the standpoint of assuring competition.
In April, the Fair Trade Commission said that by the time the cell phone unit goes public it would like NTT to reduce its stake in DoCoMo to 30 percent or less from the current 95 percent.
"It would be perfect if NTT were to cut its stake to less than 10 percent," an FTC official said.
But NTT has maintained it does not intend to cut its stake in the unit below 50 percent.

DKB's Iba said that the FTC is unlikely to be able to force NTT immediately to cut its stake in the cell phone firm to 10 percent, as it would take an enormous amount of time to prove that NTT's majority stake harms competition.
